import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

data = {
    'Sector': [
        'Public Health', 'Education', 'Urban Development', 'Transportation',
        'Rural Development', 'Environmental Sustainability'
    ],
    'Infrastructure': [75, 65, 88, 95, 80, 70],
    'Workforce Development': [85, 90, 70, 65, 78, 82],
    'Technology Adoption': [70, 80, 85, 92, 68, 88],
    'Community Engagement': [88, 78, 72, 60, 92, 85],
    'Policy Innovation': [82, 85, 78, 70, 75, 90],
    'Budget Efficiency': [78, 72, 90, 85, 80, 84]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)
sectors = df['Sector'].tolist()
categories = df.columns[1:].tolist()
values = df[categories].values

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
ax = fig.add_subplot(111, polar=True)

angles = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, len(categories), endpoint=False).tolist()
angles += angles[:1]

ax.set_theta_offset(np.pi / 2)
ax.set_theta_direction(-1)
plt.xticks(angles[:-1], categories, size=12)

ax.set_rlabel_position(0)
plt.yticks([20, 40, 60, 80, 100], ["20", "40", "60", "80", "100"], color="grey", size=10)
plt.ylim(0, 100)

colors = ['#1f77b4', '#ff7f0e', '#2ca02c', '#d62728', '#9467bd', '#8c564b']
for idx, (sector, value) in enumerate(zip(sectors, values)):
    value = np.concatenate((value, [value[0]]))
    ax.plot(angles, value, linewidth=2, linestyle='solid', label=sector, color=colors[idx])
    ax.fill(angles, value, alpha=0.25, color=colors[idx])

plt.title("Government Sector Performance Metrics (1962-1972)", size=16, y=1.1)
ax.legend(loc='upper right', bbox_to_anchor=(1.3, 1.1))

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png')

The image is a radar chart titled "Government Sector Performance Metrics (1962-1972)," which visually compares the performance of six government sectors across six distinct performance categories. The chart features a circular layout with axes radiating outward from the center, each representing one of the performance categories: Infrastructure, Workforce Development, Technology Adoption, Community Engagement, Policy Innovation, and Budget Efficiency. Concentric circular grid lines are marked at intervals of 20, 40, 60, 80, and 100 to provide a scale for measuring performance values.

Each sector is represented by a distinct colored line and filled area, making it easy to differentiate between them. The sectors included are Public Health (blue), Education (orange), Urban Development (green), Transportation (red), Rural Development (purple), and Environmental Sustainability (brown). The performance values for each sector in each category are plotted along the respective axes and connected to form a polygon, allowing for quick visual comparisons.

Public Health shows strong performance in Community Engagement (88) and Workforce Development (85) but is relatively weaker in Technology Adoption (70). Education excels in Workforce Development (90) and Policy Innovation (85) but lags in Infrastructure (65). Urban Development performs exceptionally well in Budget Efficiency (90) and Infrastructure (88), though it scores lower in Workforce Development (70). Transportation stands out in Infrastructure (95) and Technology Adoption (92) but has the lowest score in Community Engagement (60). Rural Development has a notable strength in Community Engagement (92) and performs consistently across most categories, though it is slightly weaker in Technology Adoption (68). Environmental Sustainability performs particularly well in Policy Innovation (90) and Technology Adoption (88), while its lowest score is in Infrastructure (70). The overlapping and intersecting areas of the polygons highlight the comparative strengths and weaknesses among the sectors across the different performance metrics.
